blocks.text: Huize Dina was a home for Jewish girls who could no longer live with their own  families. The home offered care, structure, and the chance to build a future within society after the girls left the home. During the Nazi occupation, Huize Dina  was forced to leave Santpoort for Amsterdam. Deportation and murder followed. Behind this history are individual lives: girls with friendships, hopes, and stories that this podcast invites us to discover.

right.caption: Girls of Huize Dina boarding a bus, from a photo album

blocks.text:
The podcast Huize Dina aims at telling the stories of some of the girls, whose archival material surfaced only recently, in 2025. The stories are told from the girls' perspective. In an imaginary, dream-like space the girls move through a hallway, opening doors that lead to memories and voices from the past.

All the text derives from the archives — but the stories are given as lived experience: where the record falls silent, the podcast listens for the voices it left out.
